chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension with associated cardiometabolic risk
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 49-year-old male with a long-standing history of essential hypertension diagnosed in 2008, now presenting with stage‑2 diastolic hypertension (DBP 107 mmHg). He has chronic obesity (BMI ≥30) since 1996 and prediabetes (A1c 6.2%) identified in 2002. Anemia has been present since 2011. Over the past few years he reports increasing psychosocial stress, ongoing intimate‑partner abuse (since 2019), and a recent shift to part‑time employment (2023), all of which may be contributing to suboptimal blood pressure control and limited lifestyle modification. He is currently on lisinopril 10 mg daily, but blood pressure remains inadequately controlled. No other cardiovascular or metabolic therapies are documented.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include prior concussions (2023), previous unemployment (2020, 2023), resolved gingival disease and gingivitis (2021), multiple medication‑review alerts (2020, 2023), and a history of reported environmental violence (2023). These reflect past acute injuries and socioeconomic instability that have since improved.
social_determinants: Part‑time employment indicating possible financial insecurity; ongoing intimate‑partner abuse and chronic stress affecting mental health and adherence; higher education may provide health literacy; limited documented social support.
risk_factor_summary: Stage‑2 hypertension (DBP 107 mmHg) despite ACE‑inhibitor therapy; obesity (BMI ≥30) and prediabetes (A1c 6.2%) place the patient at high 10‑year ASCVD risk. Anemia adds to cardiovascular strain. Charlson comorbidity index is 1 (hypertension). Polypharmacy risk is low (1 medication). Key laboratory data (BMI, lipid panel, renal function, iron studies, smoking/alcohol use) are missing, limiting precise risk quantification.

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI value is null; obesity status is inferred from diagnosis only.
Renal function not available; cannot assess CKD risk or ACE‑I safety.
Lipid profile missing; ASCVD risk calculation incomplete.
LDL cholesterol missing; statin eligibility cannot be confirmed.
Family history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or other conditions not captured.
No PHQ‑9, GAD‑7, or other mental‑health assessments despite documented stress and abuse.
Ferritin, transferrin saturation, or other iron studies absent; anemia etiology unclear.

clinical_impression: The patient presents with a high‑risk cardiometabolic profile driven by uncontrolled stage‑2 hypertension, obesity, and prediabetes, compounded by chronic anemia and significant psychosocial stressors (intimate‑partner abuse, financial insecurity). Current therapy appears insufficient, and key laboratory data are missing, suggesting gaps in risk assessment and management.
